newsitem.title: JAPAN: Keidanren head urges Japan discount rate rise-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Keidanren head urges Japan discount rate rise-Jiji.

text.p: The Japanese economy appears to be improving and it may be time to raise the official discount rate, Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the business lobby Keidanren, was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying on Thursday.
Toyoda, speaking to reporters on Japan's northernmost island of Hokkaido, was quoted by Jiji as saying: "Japan's official discount rate is at a historic low and it's unusual even by global standards.

"People who live on their savings now receive low interest payments, but small and mid-sized companies would have a hard time if interest rates rise. However, isn't it about time for a rise (in the official discount rate)?" Jiji quoted Toyoda as saying.
He said that, although it was difficult to generalise, the economy appeared to be improving according to the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.
Japan has kept its discount rate at a record-low 0.5 percent since September 1995.
